sections.h2: Where is Dubuque and what is the terrain like?
sections.html:
Dubuque is on the Mississippi River at the point where Iowa, Illinois and Wisconsin meet, an area called the Tri-State Area. It is the seat of Dubuque County and sits in the Driftless Area, a hilly region that the last glaciation skipped.

The city covers about 32 square miles and had 59,667 residents in the 2020 census, which ranked it 11th in Iowa. Median age was 37.3. The Driftless terrain is hilly, so slope is part of many lots.

When you describe a Dubuque house to a buyer, include the lot's slope and any drainage history.

sections.h2: What makes Dubuque the oldest city in Iowa?
sections.html:
Dubuque claims the title because settlement began here in 1785, when the French-Canadian trader Julien Dubuque arrived. In 1788 he received permission from the Spanish government and the Meskwaki to mine lead.

The city was chartered in 1833 and incorporated on January 28, 1857. Timber, milling, boat building and brewing grew up along the river, and the Diamond Jo Line moved its headquarters here in 1874. Waves of German, Luxembourgish and Irish Catholic immigrants arrived in the mid to late 1800s, and Dubuque became the seat of the Archdiocese of Dubuque.

Manufacturing dominated the economy until the 1980s, when industry changes and the Farm Crisis caused a steep decline. The economy broadened in the 1990s. The age of a Dubuque house is worth stating plainly when you sell.

sections.h2: How do Dubuque's four neighborhood areas differ?
sections.html:
Dubuque is usually described in four areas, each with a different housing history.

  • Downtown: the central business district, including the Fenelon Place Residential Historic District, Jackson Park, Old Main Street and the Millwork District.
  • North End: a working-class area settled by German immigrants in the late 1800s, close to Eagle Point Park, Lock and Dam No. 11 and Bee Branch Creek.
  • South End: historically Irish American, near St. Raphael's Cathedral and the Mines of Spain State Recreation Area.
  • West End: a suburban area developed after World War II, with Kennedy Mall, extending toward Asbury and Peosta.

The North End sits close to Bee Branch Creek, so its flood history is the first thing to look up.

sections.h2: Who are the largest employers in Dubuque?
sections.html:
John Deere is the largest employer in the city, followed by the school district and two hospital systems.

Tourism adds to the mix, with more than 2 million visitors a year. The Port of Dubuque redevelopment in the early 2000s brought the National Mississippi River Museum and Aquarium, a resort, a casino and a riverwalk. Loras College, Clarke University, the University of Dubuque and Emmaus University are also in the city, along with the Northeast Iowa Community College campus in Peosta.

sections.h2: What flood work has Dubuque done, and how does it affect a sale?
sections.html:
Dubuque has spent about $257.9 million on a flood mitigation plan around the Bee Branch Watershed. The city lists two detention basins (2003 and 2009), Lower Bee Branch Creek restoration (2011), Upper Bee Branch Creek restoration (2017), storm sewer upgrades and railroad culverts (2021) and a Healthy Homes program completed in 2022.

Work continues, including a gate and pump station expected around 2028, North End storm sewer improvements around 2029 and water plant flood protection around 2031. The city funded the plan partly through a $98.5 million Iowa Flood Mitigation Board award in December 2013 and $31.5 million in HUD resiliency funds in 2016.

The city has not published how many properties are protected, so a seller should ask the city and an insurer about a specific parcel rather than assume.

sections.h2: What is the Bee Branch Healthy Homes loan, and what happens if I sell?
sections.html:
The Bee Branch Healthy Homes Resiliency Program gave eligible owners a five-year forgivable loan placed as a lien on the property. If you sell during that five years, repayment may be due.

The loan carried no interest and was forgiven at 20 percent per year. Repayment comes due only if the owner sells, rents, transfers, vacates or abandons the property within the five years. The program budgeted an average of $15,067 per unit for repairs such as foundation work, sump pumps, drainage, mold remediation and furnace or water heater replacement. Owner-occupants had to keep the home as a primary residence for five years.

  • Check your title report for a city lien from this program.
  • Ask the city for a payoff or forgiveness statement before closing.
  • Income limits were tied to 80 percent of area median income when the program ran.

sections.h2: What do Dubuque rental landlords need to know before selling?
sections.html:
Dubuque requires a rental license, and the city runs a licensing and inspection program for rental housing. Fees are $45 per structure, $45 per dwelling unit and $30 per rooming unit, with a $25 late payment charge.

Since March 1, 2024, the first licensing inspection is free, while a re-inspection costs $100 per unit and a no-show costs $100 per unit. Properties in good standing can self-inspect and self-certify every other two-year cycle, with self-certification done by July 1 and fees paid by March 1. Owners must also take a Successful Property Management Course offered at NICC.

Common violations include smoke alarms, which must be outside sleeping areas, inside sleeping rooms and on every story. Carbon monoxide alarms have been required since July 1, 2018 in units with fuel-burning appliances, fireplaces or attached garages. Handrails are required on stairs with four or more steps, and guards are required where a surface is 30 inches or more above grade.

The page does not describe what happens to a license when a rental is sold. Contact Housing and Community Development, or the Inspection and Construction Services office at 563-589-4100.

sections.h2: Do Dubuque historic districts limit what a seller can change?
sections.html:
It can, depending on the address. Dubuque's Historic Preservation Commission protects historical and architectural resources, and city staff provide exterior design review. The commission has one seat for each designated historic district.

Fenelon Place and the Millwork District are among the areas downtown. If you plan to change windows, siding or other exterior features before a sale, call the commission at 50 W 13th Street, 563-589-4100, to learn whether review applies. A buyer who takes the house as is would still follow the district rules.

sections.h2: How do roads, buses and flights serve Dubuque?
sections.html:
U.S. Highways 20, 151, 52 and 61 and Iowa Highway 3 serve the city. The Julien Dubuque Bridge, built in 1943 and a National Historic Landmark, carries US 20 into Illinois, and another bridge carries US 151 toward Madison, Wisconsin.

The Jule runs the city bus system with three transfer hubs: Downtown Intermodal, Midtown and the West End. Dubuque Regional Airport has one daily flight to Chicago O'Hare. Passenger rail ended in 1981.

sections.h2: When is property tax due in Dubuque, and who handles it?
sections.html:
In Iowa the county treasurer mails the statements, and they go to the titleholder of record. The first half is due September 1 and the second March 1, with late interest starting October 1 and April 1. Taxes are normally prorated at a sale.

Owners can protest an assessment to the Board of Review between April 2 and April 30 of the assessment year, and the board cannot extend that window. Iowa's transfer tax is eighty cents per $500 above the first $500 (Iowa Code 428A.1).

faqs.q: Is Dubuque really the oldest city in Iowa?
faqs.a: Yes. Wikipedia calls it Iowa's oldest city. Julien Dubuque settled the area in 1785, the city was chartered in 1833 and incorporated on January 28, 1857.

faqs.q: How many people live in Dubuque?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 59,667 residents, which ranked Dubuque 11th among Iowa cities.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license to rent a house in Dubuque?
faqs.a: Yes. The city licenses rental structures and units, with fees of $45 per structure and $45 per dwelling unit, and inspects them.

faqs.q: What is the Bee Branch Healthy Homes loan?
faqs.a: It was a five-year forgivable loan, forgiven at 20 percent a year, for repairs in the Bee Branch Watershed. Repayment is due only if the owner sells or otherwise leaves within the five years.

faqs.q: Does Dubuque's flood project protect every house?
faqs.a: No. The city lists major work, but it does not say how many properties are protected. Check a parcel with the city and your insurer.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited Dubuque house as is?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can buy a house in its current condition, and a title company settles the taxes and liens at closing.
